Unique hydrogen environments: Let's count: methyl C1 hydrogens (3) same environment; methyl C4 hydrogens (3) maybe different; CH (C2) hydrogen (1); vinylic hydrogen? The double bond is between C2 and C3. The methyl substituent is on C3. So it's 3-methyl-2-butenoic acid. Also known as isopent-2-enoic acid? Let's check: 2-methyl-2-butenoic acid would be CH3-C(=CH2)-COOH? Not same. So our structure is 3-methyl-2-butenoic acid.

SMILES: C/C=C(C)C(=O)O? Need correct connectivity: CH3-CH=C(CH3)-COOH. Write as: CC=C(C)C(=O)O? Let's test: Starting from left CH3-CH=... So "CC=C(C)C(=O)O". That SMILES: C C = C (C) C(=O) O. That matches: first C (CH3) attached to second C (CH) which double bonds to third C (sp2) which has a methyl branch (C) and attached to carbonyl C(=O)O. Yes.

Check unique carbon count: In SMILES, there are 5 carbons. Good.
